{{Quote|The jagged scars bring thoughts of vengeance to my mind&hellip; but despite her wounds, Ska Gora still clings to the beauty she possessed before the Rakata came. When I became a ranger and all the Tython system was my home, I made excuses to visit her just to observe a world in harmony with itself.|Daegen Lok, in his holocron|<ref name="ForceWar2" />}}
The '''Holocron of Daegen Lok''' was the property of the [[Je'daii Master]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Daegen Lok]].<ref name="ForceWar2" /> In approximately [[25,792 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void]]'' dates itself to [[25,793 BBY]] and takes place while [[Daegen Lok]] is still [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Bogan]]. According to author {{Twitter|timlebbon|status/325244030705340417|[[Tim Lebbon]]|quote=@DigiFluid Sure, it's pretty much at the same time as the Force Storm arc.|archivedate=20200813210755}}, the events of the novel take place roughly concurrently to the events of [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm|''Force Storm'']], the first arc of the [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi|''Dawn of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series. Lok leaves Bogan during the second arc, [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan|''The Prisoner of Bogan'']] and the [[Dawn of the Jedi: Force War 1|first issue]] of the subsequent [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Force War|''Force War'']] arc states that one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] has passed since the previous arc's events. Therefore, the events of [[Dawn of the Jedi: Force War 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force War'' 2]] must take place in approximately [[25,792 BBY]].</ref> during the [[Invasion of the Tython system|invasion]] of the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire]], Lok recorded his thoughts relating to the [[Forest/Legends|forest]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ska Gora]] in the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] prior to participating in the [[Je'daii Order]]'s [[Attack on Ska Gora|attack]] there. Lok reflected on the natural beauty of the world and his previous experiences there as a [[Je'daii Ranger]], when he would create excuses to visit Ska Gora to admire its harmonious environment. He recalled that buildings had not been allowed to be constructed there and that floating [[City/Legends|cities]] had drifted past the planet. Lok observed that the natural environment of Ska Gora appeared to be adapting to the presence of Rakatan structures and questioned if the Je'daii were right to attack the peaceful world in order to save the rest of the [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="ForceWar2" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Holocron of Daegen Lok was quoted in [[Dawn of the Jedi: Force War 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force War'' 2]], a comic in the [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi: Force War|''Force War'']] arc of the series ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi]]''. The comic was written by [[John Ostrander]]<ref name="ForceWar2" /> and first published by [[Dark Horse Comics]] on [[December 18]], [[2013]].<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/exclusive-star-wars-comics-preview-december-titles-and-february-graphic-novels|text=Exclusive ''Star Wars'' Comics Preview: December Titles and February Graphic Novels}}</ref>
